subject: phy
title: Electronic Devices
syllabus: Semiconductors; semiconductor diode: I-V characteristics in forward and reverse bias; diode as a rectifier; I-V characteristics of LED, photodiode, solar cell and Zener diode; Zener diode as a voltage regulator. Logic gates (OR, AND, NOT, NAND and NOR).

body: E_{g}: conductor ≈ 0, semiconductor ≈ 1 eV, insulator > 3 eV; n_{e}n_{h} = n_{i}^{2}; σ = e(n_{e}μ_{e} + n_{h}μ_{h})
Pentavalent dopant (P, As) → n-type, electrons majority; trivalent (B, Al, In) → p-type, holes majority. The crystal stays neutral.
Semiconductors have a NEGATIVE temperature coefficient of resistance: hotter → more carriers → lower resistance.
Light of λ < \f{hc}{E_{g}} (hc = 1242 eV nm) creates electron–hole pairs.

Reverse current is tiny (minority carriers) and nearly constant until breakdown. The lightly doped side has the wider depletion region.

body: Half-wave: output frequency = f; full-wave/bridge: 2f. A capacitor filter smooths the ripple.
Zener: operated in reverse breakdown, holds V_{Z}: I_{S} = \f{V_{in} − V_{Z}}{R_{S}}, I_{Z} = I_{S} − I_{L}; max current \f{P_{max}}{V_{Z}}.
Photodiode: reverse biased, current ∝ light. Solar cell: no bias, large area. LED: forward biased, heavily doped, colour from E_{g}.

body: AND: 1 only if all 1. OR: 1 if any 1. NOT inverts. NAND = NOT AND, NOR = NOT OR (both universal). XOR: 1 when inputs differ; XNOR: when equal.
De Morgan: \overline{A·B} = Ā + B̄, \overline{A + B} = Ā·B̄. NAND or NOR with tied inputs is a NOT gate.
Absorption: A(A + B) = A, A + AB = A. Work any circuit row by row.

traps: Reverse current comes from MINORITY carriers.
Solar cells need a large junction area, photodiodes are reverse biased, LEDs forward biased.
Full-wave output ripples at twice the supply frequency.
A Zener only regulates if the open-circuit load voltage exceeds V_Z.

steps.note: Junctions, rectifiers, Zener, LED and solar cell

pyq.q: Conductivity of a photodiode starts changing only if the wavelength of incident light is less than 660 nm. The band gap of photodiode is found to be (\f{X}{8}) eV. The value of X is : (Given, h = 6.6 × 10^{−34} J s, e = 1.6 × 10^{−19} C)

Consider a n-type semiconductor in which n_{e} and n_{h} are number of electrons and holes, respectively. (A) Holes are minority carriers (B) The dopant is a pentavalent atom (C) n_{e}n_{h} ≠ n_{i}^{2} (where n_{i} is number of electrons or holes in semiconductor when it is intrinsic form) (D) n_{e}n_{h} ≥ n_{i}^{2} (E) The holes are not generated due to the donors
sol: Pentavalent donors add electrons, so holes become the minority (A, B true) and donors create no holes (E true).
In equilibrium n_{e}n_{h} = n_{i}^{2} still holds (mass-action law), so C and the strict form of D are false.

pyq.q: The energy needed to create a hole (excite an electron into the acceptor level) in a p-type semiconductor is 6 eV. The maximum wavelength of light which can create a hole would be : Given hc = 1242 eV nm.
sol: λ_{max} = \f{hc}{E}.

pyq.q: A light emitting diode (LED) is fabricated using GaAs semiconducting material whose band gap is 1.42 eV. The wavelength of light emitted from the LED is:
sol: ≈ 875 nm (near infrared).

pyq.q: Consider the following statements: A. The junction area of solar cell is made very narrow compared to a photo diode. B. Solar cells are not connected with any external bias. C. LED is made of lightly doped p-n junction. D. Increase of forward current results in continuous increase of LED light intensity. E. LEDs have to be connected in forward bias for emission of light.
sol: A solar cell needs a LARGE junction area to collect light (A false) and works with no external bias (B true).
LEDs are heavily doped (C false), their light saturates and they heat up as current grows (D false), and they emit only in forward bias (E true).

pyq.q: Assertion A: A diode under reverse-biased condition provides very small current which is nearly independent of voltage until a critical limit at which the current increases drastically. Reason R: Below the critical voltage limit, only majority charge carriers flow which increases drastically above critical voltage.
sol: Reverse current saturates at the tiny value I_{s} (Shockley: I = I_{s}(e^{V/V_{T}} − 1) → −I_{s}) until breakdown: A is true.
That small reverse current is carried by MINORITY carriers, not majority ones: R is false.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

pyq.q: In a semiconductor p-n diode, the doping concentrations on p-side and n-side are 10^{15} atoms/cm^{3} and 10^{18} atoms/cm^{3}, respectively. Which one of the following statements is true?
sol: The uncovered charges must balance: N_{A}x_{p} = N_{D}x_{n}.
The lightly doped p-side must spread 1000 times wider: more depletion on the p-side.
o: Widths of depletion region on either side of the interface are equal
The depletion region width is more on p-side compared to that in n-side
The depletion region width is more on n-side compared to that in p-side
No depletion region forms because of unequal doping concentrations on p and n-sides

pyq.q: A zener diode with 5 V zener voltage is used to regulate an unregulated dc voltage input of 25 V. For a 400 Ω resistor connected in series, the zener current is found to be 4 times load current. The load current (I_{L}) and load resistance (R_{L}) are :
sol: Series current = \f{25 − 5}{400} = 50 mA = I_{Z} + I_{L} = 5I_{L} → I_{L} = 10 mA.

pyq.q: In the following circuit (12 V source, 100 Ω in series, then a Zener diode of breakdown voltage 4 V in parallel with a voltmeter and a 400 Ω load with an ammeter in series with the load), the reading of the ammeter will be
sol: Without the Zener the load would get 12 × \f{400}{500} = 9.6 V > 4 V, so the Zener conducts and fixes 4 V.

pyq.q: A node is connected to +5 V through a resistor; V_{out} is taken at this node. Ideal diode D_{1} has its anode at the node and cathode at a +5 V terminal; ideal diode D_{2} has its anode at the node and cathode at ground. The output voltage is (consider ideal diode case)
sol: D_{2} is forward biased (node above ground) and, being ideal, pins the node to 0 V.
Then D_{1} sees 0 V on its anode and +5 V on its cathode: reverse biased. V_{out} = 0 V.

pyq.q: A potential divider circuit is connected with a dc source of 20 V, a light emitting diode of glow in voltage 1.8 V and a zener diode of breakdown voltage of 3.2 V (LED and Zener in series across the part PQ of the wire). The length (PR) of the resistive wire is 20 cm. The minimum length of PQ to just glow the LED is ______ cm.
sol: Across PQ we need 1.8 + 3.2 = 5 V.
The wire drops 1 V per cm, so PQ = 5 cm.

pyq.q: Which of the following circuits represents a forward biased diode? (A) anode at −10 V, cathode at 0 V; (B) anode at −10 V, cathode at −15 V; (C) anode at 4 V, cathode at 2 V; (D) cathode at −5 V, anode at −10 V; (E) cathode at 0 V (ground), anode at 2 V.
sol: Forward bias means the anode is at a higher potential than the cathode.
B (−10 > −15), C (4 > 2) and E (2 > 0) qualify; A and D have the anode lower.

pyq.q: In the given circuit, the breakdown voltage of the Zener diode is 3.0 V. A 10 V source drives a 1 kΩ series resistor, then the Zener in parallel with a 2 kΩ load. What is the value of I_{z}?
sol: Series current = \f{10 − 3}{1000} = 7 mA; load current = \f{3}{2000} = 1.5 mA.

pyq.q: Consider a circuit consisting of a capacitor (20 μF), resistor (100 Ω) and two identical diodes connected in parallel with opposite polarity, all in series with a battery. The resistance of diode under forward biasing condition is 10 Ω. The time constant of the circuit is α × 10^{−3} s. The value of α is ____.
sol: Whichever way the current flows one diode is forward biased (10 Ω) and the other is off.

pyq.q: A Zener diode of breakdown voltage 10 V is used as a voltage regulator: a 20 V source, 200 Ω in series, and a 500 Ω load across the Zener. The current through the Zener diode is
sol: Series current = \f{20 − 10}{200} = 50 mA; load = \f{10}{500} = 20 mA.

pyq.q: A diode has Zener voltage of 10 V and maximum power dissipation of 0.5 W, then the minimum resistance to be used in series with this diode for safety when it is connected to a 25 V power supply is ______ Ω.

A voltage regulating circuit consisting of Zener diode, having break-down voltage of 10 V and maximum power dissipation of 0.4 W, is operated at 15 V. The approximate value of protective resistance in this circuit is ______ Ω.

Assuming in forward bias condition there is a voltage drop of 0.7 V across a silicon diode, the current through diode D_{1} in the circuit is ______ mA. (12 V source, R_{1} = 0.3 kΩ in series, then three identical silicon diodes in parallel from the node to the return line: D_{1} and D_{3} forward biased, D_{2} reverse biased.)
sol: D_{2} is reverse biased and carries nothing; D_{1} and D_{3} conduct and hold the node at 0.7 V.
Total current = \f{12 − 0.7}{300} = 37.7 mA, shared equally: 18.8 mA each.

pyq.q: In a circuit, A and B feed an OR gate; the OR output and input A feed an AND gate whose output is C. The truth table (written as AB→C) is :
sol: C = A·(A + B).
Absorption law: A(A + B) = A, so C simply follows A.

pyq.q: In a logic circuit, A and B feed an AND gate; A is also inverted by a NOT gate; the NOT output and the AND output feed an OR gate whose output is Y. The correct truth table (Y for A B = 00, 01, 10, 11) is :
sol: Y = Ā + AB = Ā + B.
Y is 0 only when A = 1 and B = 0.

pyq.q: In a circuit, A and B feed an AND gate; Ā and B̄ (through NOT gates) feed a second AND gate; both AND outputs feed a NOR gate with output E. In the truth table, E = X for A = 0, B = 1 and E = Y for A = 1, B = 0. The values of X and Y are :
sol: E = NOT(AB + ĀB̄) — the complement of XNOR, i.e. XOR.
For unequal inputs E = 1: X = 1, Y = 1.

pyq.q: In a circuit, input A goes to a NOR gate with both its inputs tied (NOT), and B likewise; these outputs feed a NOR gate; its output goes to another NOR gate with tied inputs, giving the output. The given circuit works as :
sol: NOR with tied inputs is NOT: NOR(Ā, B̄) = AB.
The last NOT gives \overline{AB}: a NAND gate.

pyq.q: Two p-n junction diodes D_{1} and D_{2} have their anodes joined at output C, which is connected to V_{dc} = 5 V through a resistor R; their cathodes are the inputs A and B. The given circuit will function as a ____ .
sol: If either input is LOW its diode conducts and pulls C LOW.
C is HIGH only when both inputs are HIGH: an AND gate.

pyq.q: If X and Y are the inputs, each goes through a NAND gate with tied inputs; these outputs feed a NAND gate, whose output goes through another NAND gate with tied inputs to the output. The given circuit works as ______ .
sol: NAND(X̄, Ȳ) = X + Y.
The final NOT gives \overline{X + Y}: a NOR gate.

pyq.q: In a circuit, A and B feed an AND gate, and Ā and B̄ feed a second AND gate; both outputs go into gate G, whose output Y follows the truth table Y = 1, 0, 0, 1 for A B = 00, 01, 10, 11. To obtain the given truth table, the following logic gate should be placed at G :
sol: The two AND outputs are AB and ĀB̄.
Y = AB + ĀB̄ (XNOR) needs an OR gate at G.

pyq.q: In a circuit, A and B̄ feed one AND gate, Ā and B feed another AND gate, and both outputs feed an OR gate with output Y. The truth table (Y for A B = 00, 01, 10, 11) is :
sol: Y = AB̄ + ĀB: the XOR gate.
Y = 1 only when the inputs differ.

pyq.q: In a circuit, A and B̄ feed one AND gate, Ā and B feed another, and both feed an OR gate with output Y. The truth table for the circuit (Y for A B = 00, 01, 10, 11) is :
sol: Y = AB̄ + ĀB (exclusive OR).

pyq.q: Identify the logic operation performed by the given circuit: A and B each pass through a NOT gate, and the two outputs feed a NAND gate giving Y.
sol: Y = \overline{Ā·B̄}.
De Morgan: = A + B, an OR gate.

pyq.q: In a logic circuit, A and B feed an AND gate followed by a NOT gate; C and D feed an OR gate; these two outputs feed an AND gate followed by a NOT gate giving Y. The correct truth table for the inputs (A B C D) = 1101, 0011, 1010, 1111 is Y =
sol: Y = \overline{\overline{AB}·(C + D)} = AB + C̄D̄.

pyq.q: In a logic circuit, n and m feed an OR gate; the OR output and n feed a NAND gate giving z. Which of the following is the correct truth table (z for n m = 00, 01, 11, 10)?
sol: z = \overline{n(n + m)} = n̄ (absorption).
z = 1 when n = 0, else 0.

pyq.q: In a logic circuit, A goes into an AND gate with both inputs tied, B goes into a NAND gate with tied inputs followed by an AND gate with tied inputs, and the two results feed a final AND gate giving Y. Identify the correct truth table (Y for A B = 00, 01, 10, 11).
sol: AND with tied inputs passes A; NAND with tied inputs gives B̄.
Y = AB̄: 1 only for A = 1, B = 0.
